subject: Re: Brightleaf POC kickoff & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightleaf.com>, Elena Gomez <elena@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Brightleaf discovery — quick recap & proposed POC scope

Hi Samir / Elena — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed POC scope so we can align next steps.

Pain points you called out:
- High latency and cost for classification and summarization pipelines (esp. at 100k+ docs/day).
- Difficulty getting consistent outputs across prompts; frequent quality regressions after model updates.
- Security/compliance concerns around data retention and auditability for customer data.

Goals you shared:
- Reduce per-request latency by ~40% for core summarization flow.
- Cut per-token inference cost by 25% through batching/caching and model selection.
- Establish reproducible evals and monitoring for prompt/regression detection.

Proposed POC scope (3 weeks):
1) Integration: set up a private test environment (VPC peering) and ingest a sample dataset (5k documents) — our SE will handle connector and API keys.
2) Baseline & target metrics: measure current latency/cost for your summarization pipeline and set target SLOs (latency p95, tokens/sec, $/1000 tokens).
3) Prompt set + evals: run a 50-prompt evaluation set (you provide 30, Redwood adds 20) and track quality metrics (ROUGE/precision + human pass/fail).
4) Optimization: deploy batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variant; measure uplift.
5) Deliverables: POC report, configuration recommendations, and an SOW for production rollout.

Owners:
- Redwood AE: me (Marissa Cole) — overall project owner and commercial lead.
- Redwood SE: Aditya Rao — integration, test environment, eval harness.
- CS: Rishi Malhotra — success criteria and rollout plan.

Immediate asks from Brightleaf:
- Confirm the sample dataset and a secure location we can pull from (S3 or GCS).
- Provide initial 30 prompt examples for the eval set by next Wednesday (2026-12-08).
- Point of contact for IT to coordinate VPC/SSO (name/email).

I attached a one-page POC plan and a draft SOW for your review. If this looks good, we can lock dates and kick off the environment work on Monday, 2026-12-06.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
\--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132
\Attachments: brightleaf-poc-plan.xlsx, redwood-sow-draft.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir@brightleaf.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Brightleaf discovery — quick recap & proposed POC scope

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Scope: we agree with the 3-week scope and the deliverables you listed; the timeline works on our end.
2) Dataset: we will provide a 5k sample export to an S3 bucket (shared read-only creds) — ops will send details by Friday.
3) Prompts: we'll compile the 30 prompts — expect that by EOD next Wednesday (2026-12-08).
4) Security: we need SSO integration (SAML) and written confirmation of data retention policies (how long PII persists in logs/cache). Can Aditya and Rishi advise on these items?

One additional ask: can you include an A/B of two model configs (one lower-cost quantized profile + one standard) so we can compare quality vs cost? That would be useful for our finance team.

Thanks — Samir

Hi Samir / Elena — appreciate the fast turnaround. Below is the POC kickoff plan with owners, milestone dates, and specific access/setup steps.

POC kickoff plan — Brightleaf x Redwood (3 weeks)
Kickoff date: Monday, 2026-12-06
Completion target: Friday, 2026-12-24

Milestones & owners:
- Day 0-2 (Aditya): VPC peering + S3 access + SAML test user. Need IAM contact from Brightleaf to approve peering (please provide).
- Day 3-6 (Aditya + Brightleaf IT): Ingest sample dataset and run baseline tests (latency/cost).
- Day 7-10 (Aditya + Rishi): Run 50-prompt eval suite (30 provided by Brightleaf, 20 Redwood) and produce baseline quality report.
- Day 11-16 (Aditya): Deploy batching, caching, and quantized model variant — measure latency/cost delta vs baseline.
- Day 17-19 (Rishi + Marissa): Review results and produce POC report + recommendations.

Success metrics (to be measured and agreed on):
- Latency: p95 for summarization <= baseline * 0.6 (target 40% improvement).
- Cost: $/1000 tokens <= baseline * 0.75 (target 25% reduction).
- Quality: human pass rate >= baseline - 5% on critical prompts (no more than a 5% degradation on key business prompts).

Prompt set & evals:
- Please upload your 30 prompts to the shared S3 folder under /poc/prompts/ by 2026-12-08.
- Redwood will add 20 sanity-check prompts focused on edge cases and hallucination risk.
- Evaluation criteria: ROUGE-L, precision on entity extraction, and a binary human pass/fail for high-value prompts.

Access/setup checklist (Brightleaf IT):
- Create an S3 read-only IAM role for redwood-poc@redwood.ai and share role ARN.
- Provide a test SAML user for SSO verification (name/email + IdP metadata).
- Confirm IP allowlist for our test runtime (we will provide IP ranges).

Attachments included: brightleaf-poc-plan.xlsx (detailed timeline + checklist), redwood-sow-draft.pdf (non-binding).

Next steps:
- Brightleaf: share S3 details + SAML contact by 2026-12-03 (Samir indicated ops will send by Friday).
- Redwood: SE (Aditya) will initiate VPC peering setup on kickoff day; I'll follow up with a calendar invite for daily 30-min standups Mon-Fri.

If that all looks correct we will send a formal SOW and calendar invites. Happy to hop on a 15-min call if you want to walk through the checklist.

Best,
